verb.instructions: Which verb did the user ask the browser for? Choose none when the words are not a command for this page. The music verbs act on the song the appliance is playing, whatever page is open. When the words say click, press or tap — "click play", "press pause" — they name the page's own button: choose click, never a music verb.

options.navigate: go to a web address the words name: a website, a host or a url
options.search: search for the words: on the web, or on this site when they point at something on it
options.click: click one of the numbered refs on the page
options.type: type words into one of the numbered refs (a text field)
options.menu: right-click one of the numbered refs to open its menu, when no ref shown does what the words ask: the options it hides appear as new refs
options.back: go back to the previous page
options.press: press a key: enter, escape, space or an arrow key
options.read: read the page aloud or show its contents
options.clear: clear the text in the focused field
options.stop: stop what the browser is doing
options.done: this page is what the user asked for: nothing more to do
options.none: not a command for this page: a remark, a question, a name, noise
options.play: music: find a song or video on YouTube by the words and play it now — never the page's play button, which is a click
options.play_next: music: find a song by the words and play it after the one playing
options.queue: music: find a song by the words and add it to the end of the queue
options.loop: music: put the song playing on loop, so it repeats
options.loop_off: music: stop looping the song playing
options.restart: music: play the song playing again from the beginning
options.unpause: music: carry on playing the paused song
options.skip: music: skip to the next song
options.previous: music: go back to the song before
options.volume: music: set the volume to a number from 0 to 100 (the number is the words it carries)
options.show: music: show the video playing on the screen
